Surrogate

SUR-uh-gut -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, SUR; the ending sounds like 'gut,' not 'gate.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Surrogate is a substitute or replacement.

The orphaned foal accepted the gentle old mare as a surrogate mother within a week.

Worked Example

Before any new car reaches the road, the safety lab straps a sensor-filled dummy into the driver's seat and runs the crash again and again. The dummy records every force a human body would have absorbed -- so that no human body has to.

The crash-test dummy is a surrogate: a substitute that stands in for the real thing -- here, for a human passenger. A surrogate fills another's role or place, whether it is a surrogate parent, a surrogate speaker, or a stand-in measurement scientists call a surrogate for data they cannot collect directly.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

substitute: a person or thing taking another's place

stand-in: one who fills in for someone temporarily

replacement: a thing that takes the place of another

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

original: the real, first thing itself

principal: the main person, not a fill-in

Where it sits · how fully the role is taken over — stand-in → surrogate → substitute

stand-in vs. surrogate: A stand-in fills the spot briefly and steps aside when the real one returns, while a surrogate genuinely takes over the role -- a surrogate grandmother is not waiting for a replacement to arrive.

substitute vs. surrogate: Substitute is the strongest and most complete swap: a substitute fully replaces the original for as long as needed, while surrogate keeps a reminder in the air that someone else originally held the role.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sur-

prefix — sur-: in place of, under (a form of sub-) (Latin sub-)

root — rog-

root — rog-: to ask, to propose (Latin rogare)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: having been made or appointed (Latin -atus)

Put it together

Put it together: Surrogate comes from Latin surrogatus, 'asked in place of' -- sub- ('in place of') plus rogare ('to ask, to propose'). In Rome, when an official could not serve, another was formally proposed to fill the seat. A surrogate is still exactly that: someone or something appointed into a role that first belonged to another.

Use the root in a new word: submerge

Use the root in a new word: submerge: Submerge the beans completely so they can soak overnight.

Root Check

Word Choice

Surrogate usually sits right before the role it fills: a surrogate parent, a surrogate teacher, a surrogate family -- or, in science writing, 'a surrogate for' a measurement that cannot be taken directly (tree rings as a surrogate for old temperature records). It is warmer and more role-shaped than plain substitute: a surrogate does not just fill in, it takes on the relationship.
